### Type 12: Addressed Safety-Related Message

This is a point-to-point text message. The payload is interpreted as six-bit text. This message is variable in length up to a maximum of 1008 bits (up to 5 AIVDM sentence payloads).

| Field | Len | Description | Member | T | Units |
|----|----|----|----|----|----|
| 0-5 | 6 | Message Type | type | u | Constant: 12 |
| 6-7 | 2 | Repeat Indicator | repeat | u | As in Common Navigation Block |
| 8-37 | 30 | Source MMSI | mmsi | u | 9 decimal digits |
| 38-39 | 2 | Sequence Number | seqno | u | Unsigned integer 0-3 |
| 40-69 | 30 | Destination MMSI | dest_mmsi | u | 9 decimal digits |
| 70 | 1 | Retransmit flag | retransmit | b | 0 = no retransmit (default), 1 = retransmitted |
| 71 | 1 | Spare |  | x | Not used |
| 72 | 936 | Text | text | t | 1-156 chars of six-bit text. May be shorter than 936 bits. |

Pragmatic note: On [\[AISHUB\]](https://gpsd.io/AIVDM.html#AISHUB) the actual content of these messages is highly variable, ranging from fairly plain English ("PLEASE REPORT TO JOBOURG TRAFFIC CHANNEL 13") through snippets of tabular data ("PAX 589 FG 36 IX 74 MOTO 10 CREW 108+1" through what look like opaque commercial codes ("EP285 IX46 FG3 DK8 PL56") to empty strings and content that looks like line noise ("\]XFD5D/\7\`\>PA!Q DX0??K?8?\>D").

Such apparently garbled content does **not** mean there is an error in your decoder. It may indicate faulty encoders, operator error, or even the use of private encodings for non-ASCII character sets.
